messages:
Anna G (Support): FYI — Acme in prod reporting failures on function calls when they enable JSON mode. Getting 400 / validation_error. Customer says it worked earlier.
Anna G (Support): sample error from logs: \n```
validation_error: invalid_function_args: expected key 'order_ids' (array) but got string
request_id=acme-prod-req-20260317T10:12:03Z
```
Anna G (Support): attaching the request body they sent (redacted):
```
POST /v1/funcs/invoke HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "json_mode": true,
  "function": "create_shipment",
  "arguments": "{\"order_ids\": \"12345,67890\", \"destination\": {\"zip\": \"94105\"}}",
  "customer_id": "acme-corp"
}
```
Anna G (Support): note: `arguments` is a string (stringified JSON) and `order_ids` inside is a comma string — schema expects an array of strings. Customer says their SDK used to send arrays, they upgraded last week.
Mike L (Runtime): @Anna G can you paste the request_id and SDK version? also any repro script from their side?
Anna G (Support): request_id=acme-prod-req-20260317T10:12:03Z, sdk_version=2.5.0
Anna G (Support): customer provided a minimal repro (JS):
```
await redwood.callFunction({
  name: 'create_shipment',
  args: JSON.stringify({ order_ids: '12345,67890', destination: { zip: '94105' } }),
  json_mode: true
})
```
Anna G (Support): they say they didn't stringify before, but their wrapper introduced the stringify step.
Ollie (DevEx): looks like a common pitfall: SDK wrapper may auto-stringify arg objects when sending through certain proxies. @Mike L, runtime should probably catch obviously stringified JSON and parse it rather than failing hard — at least as a compatibility heuristic.
Sara M (ML): this is particularly bad for structured output because the schema validator runs after parsing. If `order_ids` becomes a single string, the function schema rejects it. We could try a defensive parse on strings that look like JSON arrays/objects.
Mike L (Runtime): checked logs: incoming Content-Type is application/json, but `arguments` field is a JSON string. The validator runs `typeof args.order_ids === 'object'` and fails. I can add a small heuristic: if `typeof arguments === 'string'` and it starts with `{` or `[` try JSON.parse once then validate. Should be low risk.
Mike L (Runtime): timeline — I'll open a bug and patch the validator. If approved, we can hotfix to canary in ~2h and full prod deploy in the next regular deploy window (~4h). Will post PR link.
Anna G (Support): can we also provide an immediate workaround for the customer? They're on a tight SLA.
Ollie (DevEx): workaround: update their wrapper to stop stringifying args OR set their code to pass arrays explicitly: `args: { order_ids: ['12345','67890'], destination: { zip: '94105' } }`. Quick stopgap: downgrade to sdk 2.4.x if that was last working.
Anna G (Support): customer asked about billing/latency impact — they had 3 retries on their side leading to extra tokens. Can we credit that? they will provide request ids for all attempts.
Mike L (Runtime): I'll annotate the issue with affected request ids. Support - please collect the list. Billing can review credits.
deploy-bot: Scheduled deploy to canary for patch: runtime/validator:try-parse-stringified-args (#4309) — will run at 14:30 UTC
Sara M (ML): small note — we shouldn't silently coerce if strict_json flag is enabled by customer. Add an opt-out header so customers who want strict validation don't get our heuristic. Maybe `X-Redwood-Strict-JSON: true`.
Mike L (Runtime): good call. We'll respect `X-Redwood-Strict-JSON` (true|false). Default remains existing (compatibility on). I'll add tests and a toggle.
Anna G (Support): copying customer on workaround and ETA. I'll update the ticket and ask for the full list of request ids for credit.
Ollie (DevEx): created internal issue: https://redwood.internal/infra/issue/RED-4309 (marked P1 for customer impact)
Mike L (Runtime): assigning to oncall and myself. I'll post PR and canary results here.
Anna G (Support): thanks all. :white_check_mark:
